memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp near
Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. They are to encamp by the sea, directly
opposite Baal Zephon.'" - Ex 14:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells them to turn back.

Look at the geography for a moment. They are to camp with the sea in front of
them and desert on either side. Militarily it is the worst possible position, a
place with no exit. And God is the one who sends them there.

This deserves our attention, because we so often assume that if we end up
trapped, we must have taken a wrong turn. Israel was exactly where God told them
to be, and it looked like a mistake.

There is a difference between a dead end we walked into through disobedience and
a dead end God led us into on purpose. The first calls for repentance. The
second calls for trust. Not every hard place is a punishment or a failure of
guidance.

Remember what came just before this: a pillar of cloud going ahead of them. They
were following visible guidance straight into an impossible position.

So before you conclude that God has abandoned you or that you have ruined
everything, ask a different question. What if He brought you here? Places with
no human exit are where God does what only God can do.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you assumed a hard place must mean you took a wrong turn?
2. What would change if you believed God led you where you are?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, when I find myself in a place with no way out, help me to trust that You
know where I am and that You led me here on purpose. Amen.
